memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Accept this atonement for your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, Lord, and do not hold your people guilty of the blood of an innocent person. Then the bloodshed will be atoned for, and you will have purged from yourselves the guilt of shedding innocent blood, since you have done what is right in the eyes of the Lord. - Deut 21:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ceremony ends with a heartfelt prayer, "Accept this atonement for your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, Lord, and do not hold your people guilty." The community pleads for God's mercy, asking Him not to charge them with this innocent blood. It is a prayer that rests entirely on God's willingness to forgive and cleanse.

Notice how they appeal to God, "whom you have redeemed." They come not on the basis of their own goodness, but on the basis of God's prior redeeming love. He had already rescued them from Egypt; now they ask Him to continue in mercy. Their hope was in the character of their redeeming God.

This is exactly how we come to God today. We do not plead our own worthiness, but the mercy of the God who has redeemed us in Christ. When guilt weighs on us, we can pray, "Accept the atonement, Lord, do not hold this against me," resting not in a broken heifer but in the finished work of Jesus. He is our atonement, and God has fully accepted His sacrifice on our behalf (1 John 2:1-2). The prayer of the ancient elders finds its true and final answer in the cross. When you feel the weight of guilt, do you come to God pleading His mercy in Christ, trusting that atonement has been made?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. On what basis do you come to God when guilt weighs on you?
2. How does resting in Christ's atonement free you from guilt?
3. What does it mean that God has accepted Jesus' sacrifice for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I come not on my own worthiness but on Your mercy in Christ. Thank You that atonement is made, and my guilt is fully covered. Amen.
